findings.text: Upheld as a defect under Q2 (duplicated logic) and Q6 (behaviour that differs from its neighbour). I checked it against the code. In learnAliases, repo.ts:658-682 writes the record with the written hash, then the file, then stages and commits. On failure it runs undoStaged and then clearIntent. This is the same failure rule as commit at store.ts:306-344. The two copies behave differently. commit wraps undoStaged and clearIntent in their own try (store.ts:332-342) and always rethrows the commit's error. At repo.ts:676-680, an error from undoStaged escapes and replaces the commit's error. The comment at 677 does not say this. Any change to the rule now has to be made in two places, and the two already disagree on which error the caller sees. A single core in repo.ts used by both callers would fix it.

Upheld as a defect under Q2 (duplicated logic, not boilerplate). I checked it against the code. opened (knowledge.ts:250-262, with isRefusal at 224-225) and rebuildAll (index-store.ts:555-566) both apply the same per-repository rule. Each opens every listed repository of the scope and skips a null. Each treats a KnowledgeError with code 'invalid' as a refusal of that one repository and goes on, and rethrows anything else. The predicate is written once as isRefusal and once inline at index-store.ts:564. This is an error classification plus a control rule, the same kind of duplication that round three upheld for the lease rule. If the set of errors counted as a refusal changes, both places must change. The architecture reviewer's F-2 reaches the same point from the contract side.
Kept as an advisory (Q3). The local named `rejected` is also the base of the accepted result at 1013. The scope is local, so this is a name that could be sharper, not one that misleads callers.
Kept as an advisory (Q5/Q8). readIntent is now a one-line forwarder to readRecord, and only tests import it.
Kept as an advisory (Q5). keepBytes' default name and its return value are used only by tests. store.ts:906 passes keptName and ignores the result.
Kept as an advisory (Q8). INTENT_OPERATIONS is still exported and nothing imports it. The rubric grades an unused export as an advisory. Carried from round three.

Kept as an advisory (Q3/Q10). The single mustBe message reads '... is not a folder; the knowledge store never follows one out of its own repository'. When the thing found is not a link, 'one' refers to nothing, and the old wording that called a gitfile 'a file, not a folder' is gone. This is wording only.

Kept as an advisory (Q11). The comments at 271 and 301-303 say 'on every system' and 'on any system'. ADR 0024 records that this was not run on Windows. These comments are new prose, not a rewrite of an older text, so they drop no fact from a previous version, and the ADR keeps the limit.
Kept as an advisory (Q3, wording). With the new max cap, the record cap prints as '65536 KiB'.
Kept as an advisory (Q2). foldersByHand and projectFolders still copy the folder listing in resolve.ts. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (Q2). adopt repeats the lease nesting in underLeases. This has been graded an advisory in earlier rounds. Carried.

Kept as an advisory (Q4/Q5). Three knobs are set only by tests: GitOptions.timeoutMs, resolveRepo's folderName and DoctorContext.gitVersion. The minimum git version is also formatted in two places. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (Q8). moduleVersion and readEntry are exported and only tests import them. Carried.
Lowered to an advisory as debt. This line is outside the change. The diff repeats the `db as Db` pattern at checks.ts:614.
Kept as an advisory (Q1). No test fails if the empty --template= is dropped from createRepository. No criterion names the template pin, and ADR 0024 states it.
Kept as an advisory (Q1). The 'not a file' half never calls openRepo after creating a folder at the record's path, so dropping `recursive` from clearIntent would leave the tests green.
Kept as an advisory (Q1). No test covers the rejected-record branch under underOwnLease while another process holds the lease, and no test covers the `started` rule.

Kept as an advisory (Q1). Three behaviours are not held by any test: catching only 'invalid', adoptAll's inner catch, and suppressing the 'nothing' line when every repository is refused. The catches in each command are held.
Kept as an advisory (Q1). No test holds the order in adoptIn where the record is written before the kept bytes.
Kept as an advisory. No test adds a file during a write's git add and commit. ADR 0024 states this as a known limit. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (Q5). The rebuild-order test depends on the internal renewal count. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (AC-8). At this level only the version probe times out. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (AC-8). 'Killed' is checked only through the 'timed out' message. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (AC-2). The parent-status check is weak. The environment test holds the ceiling guard. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (AC-13). Clipping is checked on the thrown message, not on the log line. Carried.

Kept as an advisory (AC-2). The gained-remote test resolves through the row, not through the manifest. Carried. The reviewer's open question is answered in probes/security-round-four-findings.md: with only the --ignore-submodules=all flag dropped, the nested-repository test goes red (70 pass, 1 fail, at knowledge-repo.test.ts:1525).

Upheld as a defect (Q1, boundary). I checked it against the code. refuseForeign (repo.ts:123-149) checks only the OWN_LAYOUT entries and .gitmodules, and checkRepoConfig checks only the config-type files. Nothing refuses a link elsewhere under .git/. probes/security-round-four-findings.md ran this on git 2.54.0. Case F-1 (a): with .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG linked to a file of the person's, writeEntry returned 'written', and the person's file was emptied and replaced by the commit message. Case F-1 (b): an adopt of a file whose name holds a newline put the rest of that name on a line of its own in the target file. The attacker is anyone who can drop a folder under knowledge/. With that link, they can destroy any file the person can write, and they control lines written into it, for example a shell rc file, which could lead to a program running. This is the same class that rounds two and three upheld.

Upheld as a defect (Q1 boundary; Q4 personal-data). I checked it against the code, and the same refuseForeign gap applies. probes/security-round-four-findings.md ran both variants on git 2.54.0. Case F-2 (a): with .git/logs/HEAD linked to a file of the person's, a write appended a line holding the writer's name to that file, so personal data is written outside the store. Case F-2 (b): with .git/refs and .git/objects linked into another repository, the store's commit moved that repository's main to a commit authored by 'Zoë Writer'. That is the harm ADR 0024 gives as its reason to refuse a gitfile. The attacker is the same dropper. One fix, refusing links under .git/, closes this finding and the previous one.

Kept as an advisory (availability only). dropKept's rmSync has no `recursive`, so a folder at a kept-file name throws something other than a KnowledgeError. That stops every command on the repository and the CLI's loop over repositories. The probe confirms that clearIntent's recursive rmSync removes only a link to a folder and never enters the target, so that question is closed.
Kept as an advisory (hardening). rebuildAll keeps the index rows of a repository it refuses while the folder still exists. No reader exposes them to an agent yet.

Kept as an advisory, as the reviewer graded it. keepBytes writes with no cap, but restoreKept reads under RECORD_MAX_BYTES. On an adopt of more than about 48 MiB that fails, the kept file is left behind or dropped, the person's own frontmatter is lost, and the report says 'was undone'. The entry's text survives in adopt's rewrite. Fixing the cap mismatch or the report is worth doing.

Kept as an advisory. A partial result exits 1, the same code as a total failure. A git or locked error in one repository's adopt still stops the repositories after it. ADR 0024:172 states this, and nothing reads the exit code yet.

Kept as an advisory. Rolling back across a release could drop kept bytes for an operation this binary does not know, and an unreadable record is reported as 'not one the store wrote'. ADR 0024 should say that a new operation name needs the same care as widening ALLOWED_SETTINGS.

Kept as an advisory. The three git mechanisms (the hooks path, the template and /dev/null as the global config) were run only on macOS with git 2.54.0. By the reviewer's reading, each fails closed elsewhere except a possible C:\dev\null on Windows. ADR 0024 states that this was not run on Windows.
Kept as an advisory. Leftover support folders from unreleased builds of this branch are inert and nothing removes them.

Kept as an advisory. A database where an earlier build of this branch already recorded version 6 never gets the DELETE and keeps three rows nothing reads. The backup taken before migration 6 covers the delete.
Kept as an advisory. For an adopt, 'was undone' still lists paths that were only unstaged. Carried.
Kept as an advisory. The module migration pass is not contained, and doctor does not warn when the module schema is behind. Stated as a known limit. Carried.

Kept as an advisory. The rollback is stated with its reason. It is manual, and the backup taken before the drop rotates away under BACKUPS_KEPT = 2. A refused workspace repository blocking every project write is stated in ADR 0024:172 but not in the spec's risks section. The rollback and its reason are present, so this is not a missing rollback. Carried.
Lowered to an advisory as debt. It names no line of the diff. The lint gate processing 0 files in a worktree is a tooling problem.
Lowered to an advisory as debt. The p95 flakiness predates this item and names no line of the diff.
Lowered to an advisory as debt. The upgrade runner's 10 s wait under BEGIN IMMEDIATE predates this item.
Kept as an advisory (Q6). The function-level import cycles repo-resolve and repo-author remain and are safe at runtime. This change adds none. Carried.

Kept as an advisory (Q3/Q6). The CLI and the index both decide what counts as a refusal by the generic 'invalid' code, which the module also uses for invalid input. This is within the contract in errors.ts:12 and ADR 0024:92. The duplication itself is upheld under code-quality.

Kept as an advisory. The spec's Design still describes the removed support folders and an older openRepo/doctor arrangement. ADR 0024 records the current design and declares itself the later text. Carried.
Kept as an advisory. The 64 MiB RECORD_MAX_BYTES cap is not given at ADR 0024:103, although the ADR states every other cap.
Lowered to an advisory as debt. This is outside the change: SettingKey omits two keys that SETTING_KEYS holds.
Lowered to an advisory as debt. This is outside the change: there is no forward reference to ADR 0024.

Kept as an advisory (Q3/Q5). A refused repository whose folder still exists keeps its index rows, including the person's name, until the setting is removed. ADR 0024:154 says rebuild replaces the rows and does not mention this case. One sentence in the ADR would close it. Nothing is lost.

Kept as an advisory (Q1). The DELETE of three rows of the withdrawn module is irreversible. Its reason is stated, it runs after the backup taken before migration 6, and it runs in the same transaction as the drops. The backup rotates out. probes/withdrawn-module-meta-rows.md (round-four section) addresses the reviewer's unanswered question about other writers of these keys and about releases.
Kept as an advisory (Q3). settle takes the fingerprint after the commit. This is a stated known limit. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (Q6). A one-time VACUUM INTO backup runs under the write lock on stores that ran the withdrawn module. Stated, not timed. Carried.
Kept as an advisory (Q2). project_aliases is read by project_id with no index. The table is small and the read is off the hook path. Carried.
Lowered to an advisory as debt. The missing project_id index on project_aliases predates the change.
